учиться.gloss: to study, to be a student; to learn

meanings.en: to study, to be a student; to learn
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (root 'читься'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to study', forming an aspectual pair with 'научиться'.

examples.text: Конечно, я же на ювелира учился.
examples.trans: Of course, I studied to be a jeweler, after all.

examples.text: Учись, студент, это же настоящий маркетинг!
examples.trans: Learn, student, this is real marketing!

examples.text: Но вы же с ним учились вместе!
examples.trans: But you studied together with him!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'little', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Мне камушек от бабушки в наследство достался.
examples.trans: I inherited a little stone from my grandmother.

examples.text: Так, стоять, ты куда несёшь?
examples.trans: All right, halt, where are you carrying that?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'from' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Мне камушек от бабушки в наследство достался.
examples.trans: I inherited a little stone from my grandmother.

examples.text: И что, мне теперь плясать от радости?
examples.trans: And so what, should I dance for joy now?

examples.text: Письмо от мамы.
examples.trans: A letter from Mum.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'grandmother', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Мне камушек от бабушки в наследство достался.
examples.trans: I inherited a little stone from my grandmother.

examples.text: Моя бабушка живёт в деревне.
examples.trans: My grandmother lives in the village.

examples.text: Это лучше, чем бабушка.
examples.trans: That's better than the old lady.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'grandmother'.

examples.text: Мне камушек от бабушки в наследство достался.
examples.trans: I inherited a little stone from my grandmother.

достаться.gloss: to fall to, to get punished/scolded

meanings.en: to fall to, to get punished/scolded
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (root 'статься'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fall to', forming an aspectual pair with 'доставаться'.

examples.text: Мне камушек от бабушки в наследство достался.
examples.trans: I inherited a little stone from my grandmother.

examples.text: Нам сильно достанется от шефа.
examples.trans: We will really get it from Chef.

examples.text: Точно, иначе нам сильно достанется!
examples.trans: Exactly, otherwise we will really get it!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'лушать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to listen', forming an aspectual pair with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, ну не обижай её, а.
examples.trans: Listen, do not offend her, huh.

examples.text: Слушай, продай мне, сто тысяч дам!
examples.trans: Listen, sell it to me, I will give you a hundred thousand!

examples.text: Слушай, вообще-то сейчас ночь на дворе.
examples.trans: Listen, it is actually the middle of the night outside.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian num meaning 'a hundred', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В четверг банкет на сто человек.
examples.trans: On Thursday there is a banquet for a hundred people.

examples.text: Какой ещё банкет на сто человек?
examples.trans: What banquet for a hundred people?

examples.text: Банкета на сто человек не будет.
examples.trans: There will not be a banquet for a hundred people.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'thousand', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Слушай, продай мне, сто тысяч дам!
examples.trans: Listen, sell it to me, I will give you a hundred thousand!

examples.text: Значит, он все триста тысяч стоит!
examples.trans: That means it is worth a full three hundred thousand!

examples.text: Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give', forming an aspectual pair with 'давать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Я тебе на пробу дам бесплатно.
examples.trans: I will give you one to try for free.

examples.text: Слушай, продай мне, сто тысяч дам!
examples.trans: Listen, sell it to me, I will give you a hundred thousand!

examples.text: Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: Give me just one.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'so'.

examples.text: Значит, ты не придёшь?
examples.trans: So you're not coming?

examples.text: Значит, всё.
examples.trans: So that's it.

examples.text: Значит, сделай так, чтобы забрал.
examples.trans: Then make sure he does.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian num meaning 'three hundred', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Значит, он все триста тысяч стоит!
examples.trans: That means it is worth a full three hundred thousand!

examples.text: А для него это как триста!
examples.trans: And for him it's like three hundred!

examples.text: Билет стоит триста рублей.
examples.trans: The ticket costs three hundred roubles.
